Option O1 references missing risk Linear accumulation of artifacts can pressure context-window bounds if context-pack selection is not strict.
Option O1 references missing risk Flaky validator behavior can exhaust retry budgets and stall the only active lane.
Option O2 references missing risk Merge conflicts between lanes may be frequent in tightly-coupled repos, driving escalation rates.
Option O2 references missing risk Missed dependencies in task partitioning can cause late integration failures and rework.
Option O2 references missing risk Reproducibility depends on merge ordering rules that must be independent of wall-clock completion timing.
Option O2 references missing risk Workspace partition boundaries can be violated by side-effecting tools unless sandboxing and path scoping are strict.
Option O3 references missing risk Validation cost may pressure teams to weaken regression gates, reducing safety.
Option O3 references missing risk Environment drift between runs can break deterministic replay/resume unless toolchains are pinned.
Option O3 references missing risk Budget thresholds for partial-freeze decisions can be misestimated, freezing too early/late.

Option O4 references missing risk Internal complexity may grow and undermine CNS12 separation (reviewers/judges becoming entangled with writing/patching).

Option O4 references missing risk Monolith becomes a high-blast-radius component for failures and changes.

Decision reference missing: Parallel lane partitioning is derived from the work_plan.json dependency DAG; only tasks with no cross-lane dependencies are assigned to separate lanes, minimizing merge conflict risk (K12).

Decision reference missing: Each lane operates in a namespaced workspace partition (C22) with scoped tool permissions and file-path restrictions enforced by the Task Lane Orchestrator (C13), preventing cross-lane contamination.

Decision reference missing: Integration merge ordering is deterministic and independent of wall-clock lane completion timing; patchsets are applied in a canonical order derived from the work_plan DAG, not arrival order.

Decision reference missing: The Integration stage (C18→C19→C20→C21) is a dedicated sub-flow with its own validation, review, and repair cycle; merge conflicts exceeding deterministic resolution thresholds trigger structured conflict reports and escalation (HITL or reroute).

Decision reference missing: Medium HITL strictness: HITL is triggered for unresolved merge conflicts, critical security findings, secrets detection, protected-path modifications, ChangeRequests, gate waivers, and integration-level critical findings; lane-level validation relies more on automated gates.
Decision reference missing: Writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor diversity are enforced by the Global Orchestrator (C11) routing policy across all lanes and integration stages.
Decision reference missing: Context packs are compiled per-lane (scoped) and per-integration-stage (full integrated state) by the orchestrator using deterministic selection rules with bounded size.

Decision reference missing: Acceptance is two-tiered: each lane must pass its scoped gates (build/test/lint per lane file set) before fan-in; the integrated state must pass full-repo validators, integration review, and all freeze closure gates before the bundle is released.
